prerequisites: Some exposure to formal languages, logic and programming
description: An understanding of formal logic. Familiarity with representations for several core domains. Hands-on experience creating and using knowledge representations.

syllabus.title: Logic Foundations
syllabus.body: Propositional logic: syntax and semantics, proof systems, natural deduction, tableau method, resolution method; First Order Logic (FOL): syntax and semantics, unification, forward chaining.

syllabus.title: Rule-Based and FOL Representation
syllabus.body: The Rete algorithm, programming rule based systems, representation in FOL, categories and properties, reification, event calculus, deductive retrieval, backward chaining, logic programming with Prolog.

syllabus.title: Description Logic
syllabus.body: Resolution refutation in FOL, FOL with equality, complexity of theorem proving, Description Logic (DL), structure matching, classification, the ALC language, inheritance in taxonomies.

syllabus.title: Non-monotonic Reasoning
syllabus.body: Default reasoning, circumscription, the event calculus revisited, default logic, autoepistemic logic, epistemic logic, multi agent scenarios.

outcomes: Describe, apply and demonstrate syntactic and semantic formal models for natural language processing.
Apply and demonstrate knowledge-based learning methods.
Write Prolog programs to solve automated reasoning tasks and explain how they will execute.
Apply reasoning techniques (transformation to clausal form, resolution, saturation) to establish properties of first-order problems.
textbooks: Ronald J. Brachman, Hector J. Levesque, Knowledge Representation and Reasoning, Morgan Kaufmann, 2004.
Deepak Khemani, A First Course in Artificial Intelligence, McGraw Hill Education (India), 2013.
